name: Chisapani
tagline: Cold water, oak forest and the Himalaya one walk from Kathmandu
meta_description: Chisapani at 2,200 m: first night of the Helambu trek, a 4–5 hour walk from Sundarijal through Shivapuri forest, with sunrise views of Langtang.
summary: Chisapani is a small lodge village at about 2,200 m on the north side of the Shivapuri ridge, the first overnight stop on the Helambu trek. It is 4 to 5 hours' walk from Sundarijal on the edge of Kathmandu, and on clear mornings looks across to Langtang, Jugal and Ganesh Himal.
intro: Chisapani means cold water in Nepali, and the name fits: a spring on the ridge gave travellers fresh water long before the lodges came. The village sits at about 2,200 m just north of the rim of the Kathmandu Valley, inside Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park. It is the closest place to Kathmandu where you can sleep in a trekking lodge and wake up to a line of snow peaks.

Most people walk here from Sundarijal, at the north-eastern edge of the city, climbing beside the old water pipeline, past the reservoir dam and through oak forest to the pass at Borlang Bhanjyang. The walk takes 4 to 5 hours. From Chisapani, the Helambu trail continues north to Kutumsang and Tharepati, or you can turn east to Nagarkot and back to the valley.

Chisapani was badly damaged in the 2015 earthquake, and its lodges were rebuilt in the following years. It is not a traditional village so much as a trekkers' stop with a small Tamang and Brahmin farming community around it. For travellers short of time, a single night here is the easiest real taste of the Nepali hills from Kathmandu. It works well at the start or end of a longer trip.

story.title: A spring on the ridge above the valley
paras: For centuries people walking between the Kathmandu Valley and the hill villages to the north crossed the Shivapuri ridge. The route through Sundarijal and Borlang Bhanjyang was one of the easier crossings, and the spring at Chisapani was a natural resting point. Porters carrying goods to and from Helambu, and later Hyolmo traders and pilgrims to Gosaikunda, stopped here for water and shelter. The walk took most of a day from the valley floor, so travellers going north usually slept at or near the ridge before the long descent toward the Melamchi and Talamarang valleys. In that sense Chisapani has always been a first night out of Kathmandu.

The ridge above has its own importance. Shivapuri hill, at 2,732 m, is the highest point on the valley rim and the catchment of the Bagmati river, which rises at Baghdwar in these forests. In the 20th century the hills were protected first as a watershed for Kathmandu's drinking water; the Sundarijal reservoir and its hydroelectric station are part of that history. In 2002 the area was gazetted as Shivapuri National Park, Nepal's ninth national park, later extended to include the Nagarjun forest.

Trekking lodges grew at Chisapani from the 1970s as Helambu became a popular short trek. The 2015 earthquake damaged or destroyed most of them, and owners rebuilt, some in concrete and some in stone. Rough jeep roads now reach the ridge, but the walk from Sundarijal is still the best way to arrive: you feel the city fall away behind you. Lodge owners here depend on the autumn and spring seasons, and on Kathmandu families who come up for weekends and holidays. The view, the cold water and the quiet forest are what they sell, and on a clear morning it is easy to see why people keep coming back.

people: The settlements around Chisapani are mainly Tamang, with some Brahmin and Chhetri families. People farm maize, millet and vegetables on terraces below the ridge, keep buffaloes and goats, and run the lodges. Many households have members working in Kathmandu, an hour or two away by road, and the area's life is closely tied to the city.

untold.fact: Shivapuri hill above Chisapani, at 2,732 m, is the highest point on the rim of the Kathmandu Valley, and the national park named after it was gazetted in 2002 as Nepal's ninth national park.
Sundarijal, where the walk to Chisapani begins, has a small dam and hydroelectric station and is also the headquarters of Nepal's Himalayan Rescue Dog squad.
The forests of Shivapuri form an important water catchment, supplying the Kathmandu Valley daily, and the Bagmati, Kathmandu's sacred river, rises in these hills at Baghdwar.

local_words.meaning: Cold water, the source of the village name
Pass or saddle on a ridge, as in Borlang Bhanjyang

taste.name: Dal bhat with buckwheat roti
taste.text: Chisapani lodges serve generous dal bhat with refills of rice, lentils and vegetable curry. Ask if they have buckwheat (phapar) roti, a dark, nutty flatbread from the hill farms, served with honey or chilli pickle. Eat on the terrace at sunset with the peaks in view.

facts: Sunrise over Langtang and Jugal, first night of Helambu

highlights.title: Sunrise over the Himalaya
highlights.text: On clear mornings, from October to February especially, the view from Chisapani stretches from Ganesh Himal across Langtang to Jugal Himal. Get up before 6 am and stand on the lodge terraces as the peaks turn gold.

highlights.title: The walk from Sundarijal
highlights.text: A 4 to 5 hour climb from the edge of Kathmandu, beside the water pipe, over the dam and through oak and rhododendron forest to the valley rim at Borlang Bhanjyang. It is a real hill walk without leaving the city behind for long.

highlights.title: Shivapuri forest
highlights.text: The national park around Chisapani has oak, rhododendron and pine forest, more than 300 bird species and mammals such as barking deer and leopard, which are rarely seen. Walk quietly in the early morning for birds.

highlights.title: Gateway to Helambu
highlights.text: Chisapani is the first night of the Helambu trek. From here the trail runs north along the ridge to Kutumsang and Tharepati and into the Hyolmo villages, or across Lauribina La to Gosaikunda. Many trekkers sleep here on the first and last nights of the trek.

highlights.title: Down to Nagarkot
highlights.text: From Chisapani a day's walk east through farm villages leads to Nagarkot, a hill resort on the valley rim. It makes a good two-day loop from Kathmandu with two sunrise views. Your guide can arrange a car from Nagarkot back to Kathmandu.

how_to_reach.text: Drive about 15 km, 45 minutes, from Thamel to Sundarijal, then walk 4 to 5 hours via the reservoir, Mulkharka and Borlang Bhanjyang. Pay the national park fee at the gate.
Rough jeep tracks reach Chisapani in dry weather, about 3 to 4 hours from Kathmandu depending on the route. Monsoon rain can make them impassable.

where_to_stay: Chisapani has a cluster of lodges rebuilt after 2015, most with twin rooms, shared or attached bathrooms, hot showers from gas or solar heaters, and dining rooms with mountain views. Standards are simple but better than higher on the trail. Choose a lodge on the north side of the ridge for sunrise views from the room. At weekends and Nepali holidays, groups from Kathmandu can fill lodges, so book ahead in October and November.
tips: Start from Sundarijal by 9 am to arrive in daylight; the forest section is dark early in winter.
Do not walk the Sundarijal–Chisapani trail alone; go with a guide or in a group.
Carry the Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park ticket; rangers check it on the trail.
Bring a warm layer even in spring; mornings at 2,200 m are cold before sunrise.
Avoid Friday and Saturday nights in peak season if you want a quiet lodge.

experiences.title: Hike from Sundarijal to Chisapani
experiences.summary: Leave the city on foot: climb from Sundarijal beside the old water pipeline, over the reservoir dam, through Mulkharka and oak forest to the valley rim at Borlang Bhanjyang, then down to Chisapani for the night. It is the classic first day of Helambu.
body: The trail starts where the road ends at Sundarijal, at about 1,390 m. The first hour is a long stone staircase beside the large water pipe that has fed Kathmandu for decades, with the stream below. After about 40 minutes you cross the dam of the reservoir, then climb through forest on the national park's watershed road. The water pipeline and reservoir were built to supply Kathmandu, and the area around them is protected watershed. Go at your own pace on the stairs; there are plenty of places to stop and look back over the city as it shrinks below you.

Mulkharka, a scattered Tamang village at about 1,900 m, has tea shops and a view back over the Kathmandu Valley. From here the path continues up through oak forest, past an army post and into Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park, to the pass at Borlang Bhanjyang at about 2,400 m on the rim of the valley. Mulkharka is the last place for a proper tea stop before the pass, so rest here, refill water and buy snacks. Park rangers may check your ticket at the army post or gate, so keep it within easy reach rather than buried in your pack.

From the pass, the trail drops gently through forest and fields to Chisapani. In spring rhododendrons flower red along the way. Arrive by mid-afternoon, take a hot shower and wait for the sunset light on the peaks to the north. Lodges at Chisapani have hot showers, simple rooms and dining rooms with views, and dal bhat is ready by early evening. Nights are cold from November to February, near freezing, so keep a warm layer handy for the terrace. Go to bed early; sunrise is the main event.

faqs.q: Is the Sundarijal to Chisapani hike steep?
faqs.a: The first hour from Sundarijal is a steep staircase, and the trail climbs about 1,000 m in total to Borlang Bhanjyang, then descends a little to Chisapani. Overall it is a moderate day hike of 4 to 5 hours. Take it slowly, drink water and use walking poles if your knees are sensitive.

faqs.q: Is it safe to walk to Chisapani alone?
faqs.a: We advise against it. The forest section north of Mulkharka is quiet, and there have been rare incidents involving lone walkers in the past. Walk with a guide or at least in a group. A licensed guide is also required for foreign trekkers in national parks under the rule in force since April 2023; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much is the Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park fee?
faqs.a: Foreign visitors pay an entry fee at the park gate near Sundarijal, with lower rates for SAARC and Nepali citizens. The amount changes from time to time, so check current status before you travel. Keep the ticket with you, as rangers check it on the trail and at Chisapani.

experiences.title: Sunrise panorama from Chisapani
experiences.summary: Wake before dawn to watch the sun rise over a 200 km stretch of Himalaya, from Ganesh Himal through Langtang to Jugal, from the terraces and ridge above Chisapani. No trekking needed beyond the walk up.
body: Chisapani faces north across the Melamchi and Talamarang valleys to the main Himalayan chain. On a clear morning you see Ganesh Himal to the west, the Langtang range in the centre, and Jugal Himal and Dorje Lakpa to the north-east, often with cloud lying in the valleys below. The best months for this view are October to February, when the air is dry and haze is low. In spring, peaks are often visible only for the first hour after sunrise before haze rises from the valleys. In the monsoon, the view is usually hidden altogether.

Step out of the lodge at about 5.45 am in autumn, or 6.15 am in winter, with a warm jacket and a cup of tea. The first light touches the highest snow peaks, which turn pink, then gold, then white over about 20 minutes. Many lodges have rooftop terraces; the small rise behind the village is even better. Bring a light tripod if you want long-lens shots of the peaks, as the cold makes hands unsteady. Even with a phone, the changing colour of the snow is worth recording. Stay a few minutes after the sun clears the ridge to see the valleys below light up.

Your guide can name the peaks and point out where the treks of Langtang and Helambu run. After sunrise, breakfast, and either continue north to Helambu or walk east to Nagarkot. If cloud hides the view on your morning, ask your lodge if you can wait an hour; it often clears briefly. Many trekkers plan two nights at Chisapani in winter simply to have two chances at the sunrise, and the second morning is often the clearer one.

faqs.q: Can you see Everest from Chisapani?
faqs.a: No, not reliably. Chisapani's view is of the central Himalaya: Ganesh Himal, Langtang, Jugal and Dorje Lakpa. Everest lies far to the east and is generally hidden by nearer ranges and haze. For a distant Everest view near Kathmandu, Nagarkot on a very clear winter morning gives a small chance.

faqs.q: What month gives the best views from Chisapani?
faqs.a: October to February, after the monsoon has washed the air clean and before spring haze builds. November and December are the most reliable. In March and April views are often hazy by mid-morning, and from June to September cloud usually hides the peaks completely.

faqs.q: What time is sunrise at Chisapani?
faqs.a: In October sunrise is around 6 am, in December and January about 6.45 am, and in April about 5.45 am. Get up 20 to 30 minutes earlier for the first light on the peaks. Mornings are cold, around 0 to 5 °C in winter, so dress warmly.

experiences.title: Walk from Chisapani to Nagarkot
experiences.summary: A long day's walk east from Chisapani through farm villages and forest along the valley rim to the hill resort of Nagarkot, for a second sunrise. A classic two-day loop from Kathmandu. Expect ups and downs rather than one big climb.
body: From Chisapani the trail drops east through terraced farmland to Chauki Bhanjyang and Jhule, small Tamang and Brahmin villages where life follows the farming year. You walk on village paths and some dirt roads, past houses with maize hanging under the eaves and buffaloes in the yards. The villages along the way see fewer trekkers than the Helambu trail itself, and people are curious and friendly. Tea shops are simple; your guide will know which ones serve a good lunch of dal bhat or noodles. Carry enough water for the stretches between them.

The route then climbs again through pine and rhododendron forest along the rim of the Kathmandu Valley to Nagarkot at about 2,100 m. It is longer than the walk up from Sundarijal, 6 to 7 hours, with ups and downs rather than one big climb. In spring this part of the walk is bright with rhododendrons, and in winter the views north to the Himalaya follow you much of the way. Some sections follow jeep roads, which are dusty in dry months, but the forest trail near Nagarkot is shaded and pleasant.

Nagarkot has many hotels and a viewpoint tower for sunrise, with a broad Himalayan view from Langtang east toward the Everest ranges on very clear days. Next morning, drive back to Kathmandu in about 1.5 hours or walk down to Bhaktapur. From Nagarkot you are only about 30 km from Kathmandu, so this walk turns Chisapani into a tidy two-day loop with two sunrise views. It is a good option for travellers who want a taste of trekking without committing to a full week in the hills.

faqs.q: How far is Chisapani from Nagarkot?
faqs.a: The walking route is roughly 20 km and takes 6 to 7 hours with breaks. It follows village paths, some jeep roads and forest trails, with several climbs and descents. Start soon after breakfast and carry lunch, as tea stops are limited between villages.

faqs.q: Is the Chisapani to Nagarkot walk suitable for children?
faqs.a: For active children of 10 or older who walk regularly, yes, with breaks. It is a long day. Younger children may manage with shortcuts by jeep for part of the way. Bring snacks, sun protection and enough water, and keep a steady, unhurried pace.

faqs.q: Where do I stay in Nagarkot?
faqs.a: Nagarkot has a wide range of hotels and resorts along the ridge, from simple guesthouses to comfortable resorts with mountain-view rooms. We choose based on your budget and the view. It is about 1.5 hours by road from Kathmandu, so you can return the next morning after sunrise.

experiences.title: Early bird walk in Shivapuri forest
experiences.summary: Walk the oak and rhododendron forest around Chisapani at first light with a birding guide, looking for laughingthrushes, minivets, barbets and other species of the Himalayan foothills. Bring binoculars. A good add-on for keen naturalists.
body: Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park protects the forested hills on the north rim of the Kathmandu Valley, and its mix of oak, rhododendron and pine supports a large bird list, with more than 300 species recorded in the park. Chisapani, on the northern edge, is a good base for an early walk. The park also protects the catchment that supplies part of Kathmandu's drinking water, so its forests are some of the best preserved close to the city. Walking quietly in them at dawn feels a world away from the traffic below.

We set out at dawn along quiet forest trails near the village. Typical sightings include laughingthrushes, minivets, barbets, woodpeckers and, in winter, flocks of tits and warblers that move through the canopy. Kalij pheasants feed on the forest floor early in the morning. A local birding guide knows the calls and the best spots for each species, and makes a huge difference. Without one, you may hear far more birds than you see. Morning light filters through the oaks, and the forest is at its liveliest in the first two hours.

Mammals such as barking deer, macaques and squirrels are possible, while leopards live in the park but are rarely seen. Bring binoculars and dull-coloured clothes, and move slowly. Back for breakfast by 9 am, before continuing your walk. Keep to the trails, do not play recorded calls to attract birds, and avoid feeding monkeys. Leave no litter: the park's rangers and local volunteers work hard to keep the trails clean. A slow walk is the whole point; there is no summit to reach.

faqs.q: What birds can I see near Chisapani?
faqs.a: Common sightings include laughingthrushes, minivets, barbets, woodpeckers, bulbuls and, in winter, mixed flocks of tits and warblers. Kalij pheasants are often seen at dawn. The park has more than 300 recorded bird species. A local birding guide improves your chances considerably.

faqs.q: Are there leopards in Shivapuri forest?
faqs.a: Yes, leopards live in Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park, but they are shy and rarely seen by walkers. Barking deer, rhesus macaques and squirrels are more likely. Walk in a group with a guide, keep to marked trails and avoid walking in the forest after dark.

faqs.q: When is the best season for birding at Chisapani?
faqs.a: October to May, with March to May busy with breeding birds and singing, and winter bringing flocks of altitudinal migrants down from higher forests. Early morning is always best. Bring binoculars; few lodges have any to lend. Spring mornings bring the most song.

faqs.q: Where is Chisapani?
faqs.a: Chisapani is on the northern side of the Shivapuri ridge, just outside the rim of the Kathmandu Valley, at about 2,200 m. It lies in Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park and is the first overnight stop on the Helambu trek, 4 to 5 hours' walk from Sundarijal on Kathmandu's north-eastern edge.

faqs.q: How do I get to Chisapani from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Take a car or taxi about 15 km, 45 minutes, from Thamel to Sundarijal, then walk 4 to 5 hours up through the national park via Mulkharka and Borlang Bhanjyang. Jeeps can reach Chisapani on rough roads in dry weather. Walking is the best way to arrive.

faqs.q: Is Chisapani good for a one-night trek from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of the best short trips from the city. Walk up from Sundarijal, sleep in a lodge, watch the sunrise over Langtang and Jugal, then walk back down or on to Nagarkot. It needs only two days and no long drives or flights.

faqs.q: What is the altitude of Chisapani?
faqs.a: About 2,200 m, roughly 900 m higher than Kathmandu. Altitude sickness is not a concern at this height for healthy people. The highest point on the walk from Sundarijal is Borlang Bhanjyang, at about 2,400 m, just before Chisapani. You may feel slightly more breathless on the climb than in the city, but nothing more.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to visit Chisapani?
faqs.a: Yes. Chisapani is inside Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park, which charges an entry fee to foreigners, paid at the Sundarijal gate. Since April 2023, foreign trekkers in national parks are required to go with a licensed guide. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Was Chisapani affected by the 2026 flood?
faqs.a: No. Chisapani lies on the Shivapuri ridge north of Kathmandu, far from the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers that flooded on 26 August 2026. The walk from Sundarijal and the lodges were not affected. As always, monsoon landslides can damage jeep roads; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Chisapani?
faqs.a: October to February for clear mountain views, and March and April for rhododendrons and warm days, though haze is common. Avoid June to September, when rain, leeches and cloud spoil both the walk and the view. Winter nights drop near freezing.

faqs.q: Are there good lodges in Chisapani?
faqs.a: Chisapani has several simple lodges, rebuilt after the 2015 earthquake, with twin rooms, some attached bathrooms, hot showers and dining rooms with mountain views. Do not expect hotel standards. Book ahead for weekends and Nepali holidays in October and November, when groups from Kathmandu arrive.

faqs.q: Can families with children do the Chisapani trek?
faqs.a: Yes. It is a good first trek for children of about 8 and older who walk regularly, with a single climb of 4 to 5 hours and a comfortable lodge night. Younger children can manage with carrying help or a jeep ride. Bring warm clothes for the cold morning and plenty of snacks.
